findings.title: Working-hours check rejects valid slots when a day has multiple working-hour ranges
findings.body:
`workingHours.find(...)` returns true as soon as any single working-hour entry for that weekday does not contain the slot, and the slot is then rejected. Take a schedule with split hours on one day, e.g. 9–12 and 13–17. A 14:00 slot is outside 9–12, so it is marked unavailable even though it falls inside 13–17. The same happens when one range is split across UTC days.

This check now runs for every fixed host, which includes all users of personal and collective events. Legitimate availability will disappear from booking pages. The check should require that the slot is contained in at least one range (`some` contains), not reject on the first range that doesn't contain it.

findings.title: Slot end computed from slot start in working-hours check
findings.body: `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start`. It should use `slotEndTime`. As written, a slot that starts inside working hours but runs past the end of them passes the check, so the end-of-day boundary is never enforced.

findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === so the empty-override case never matches
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares two freshly created object references, so it is always false. A zero-length date override (the way a fixed host marks a whole day unavailable) is therefore never detected as fully blocking. A slot overlapping that instant falls through and is treated as available. Use `.isSame()` or compare `valueOf()`.

findings.title: Override containment check misses slots extending past override end and slots starting exactly at end
findings.body:
A slot is rejected only if it ends at or before the override start, or starts strictly after the override end.

- A slot starting exactly at the override end passes, because `isAfter` is false when the times are equal.
- A slot that starts inside the override but ends after it also passes.

In round-robin, slots are generated from all hosts' availability. So a fixed host can be booked partly or wholly outside their date override, which is the bug this PR set out to fix. The check should require `slotStart >= overrideStart && slotEnd <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Override day matching mixes timezones and is UTC-date based
findings.body:
The override's day is taken from `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format(...)`, which formats in the server's local timezone. The slot's day comes from `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is in UTC. On non-UTC servers these can disagree.

Matching on UTC dates is also problematic. For organizers far from UTC, an override on local day D can start on UTC day D-1. When that happens:

- Regular slots on UTC day D-1 outside the override are wrongly rejected.
- Day D falls back to normal working hours, ignoring the override.

findings.title: Offset-shifted override times wrap at midnight and are matched to the wrong day
findings.body:
After applying `offset`, only `hour()`/`minute()` are used, so a shifted override that crosses midnight wraps around. For example, 20:00–23:00 shifted by +3h becomes 23:00–02:00, i.e. startTime 1380 and endTime 120. `buildSlots` skips it because start >= end, so the override vanishes.

Separately, `activeOverrides` (line 207) selects overrides using the unshifted `override.start`. An override that moves into the next or previous invitee day after the offset is still applied to the original day.
